one_liner: Pay-as-you-go SEO data APIs: SERPs, keywords, backlinks, on-page, AI/LLM visibility data.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic auth with an API login + auto-generated API password from the dashboard's API Access tab (differs from account password). Base64(login:password) in Authorization header; credentials cannot be passed as URL params. No separate API key or OAuth for the REST API.
access_notes: Self-serve signup gives API credentials, a free Sandbox (sample responses, no real data) and a $1 trial credit. Real data beyond the trial is pay-as-you-go with a $50 minimum top-up; balance never expires. No subscription.
api_breadth_notes: ~12 API families (SERP, AI Optimization, Keywords Data, DataForSEO Labs, Backlinks, OnPage, Content Analysis, Domain Analytics, Merchant, App Data, Business Data, Databases); roughly 400+ endpoint pages by menu count (SERP alone ~125). Standard (task post/get) and Live modes.
mcp_notes: Official remote server https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp (Basic auth header, OAuth-style prompt in some clients) plus local npx package dataforseo-mcp-server / Docker dataforseo/mcp; source github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript.
notes: Docs appendix lists Sandbox and Webhook Resend pages and a Help Center article on webhooks/callbacks (task-based Standard mode delivers results via callbacks); exact pingback/postback parameter docs were not opened. Live mode costs more than Standard. Endpoint count is an approximation from the docs menu. Basic auth means toolkit stores login+password pair per user.

one_liner: SEO platform: rank tracking, keyword/backlink/domain data, site audit, local and AI-search visibility.
auth_notes: API key from API Dashboard sent as 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' (or apikey/token query param). One key now works for both Data API and Project API. Base URL https://api.seranking.com. Hosted MCP additionally supports OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration or X-Api-Key header; no OAuth for the REST API documented.
access_notes: 14-day free trial with 100K API credits and MCP access, no credit card. Afterwards paid: Data API credits via Wallet top-ups, Standalone ($179/mo billed annually, Data API only) or an add-on ($29/mo+) to Core/Growth/Enterprise subscriptions (add-on includes Project API). Project API calls consume subscription limits.
api_breadth_notes: Four APIs: Data API (backlinks, domain analysis, keyword research, AI search, website audit, account), Project API (~15 groups: projects, keyword groups, competitors, analytics, audit, backlink checker, AI results tracker...), Local Marketing API (~7 groups), SE Visible API (beta, ~9 groups). Likely 100+ operations.
mcp_notes: Official hosted remote server https://api.seranking.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 or X-Api-Key). Covers Data, Project, Local Marketing and SE Visible APIs; tools depend on subscription. No official GitHub repo linked on the page.
blocker: API credits paid after 14-day free trial
notes: Rate limit: 5 req/s per method, repeated 429s trigger a 10-minute block. Pricing figures differ across regional pricing pages and an older help page still describes separate Data/Project keys and Project API restrictions on Essential/Pro plans; verify current plan gating. MCP API keys currently have full account access (no read-only keys).

one_liner: SEO toolset: backlinks, keywords, site audit, rank tracking, brand radar and web analytics data.
auth_notes: API v3 key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Keys created only by workspace owners/admins (Account settings > API keys), up to 1,000 per workspace, expiry configurable up to 10 years. OAuth2 exists only via the Ahrefs Connect integration program (apply + app review). A few 'public' endpoints need no key.
access_notes: API v3 available on paid plans Lite and higher (Lite 200K units/mo, Standard 800K, Advanced 2M, Enterprise custom); every request costs at least 50 units. Free test queries (targets ahrefs.com/yep.com/firehose.com) cost 0 units but still require a paid-plan API key. No free plan path to API credentials.
api_breadth_notes: 15 per-tool OpenAPI specs: Site Explorer, Competitive Analysis, Keywords Explorer, Site Audit, Rank Tracker, SERP Overview, Batch Analysis, Subscription Info, Management, Brand Radar, Content Helper, Web Analytics, GSC Insights, Social Media, Public. Exact endpoint count not stated (likely 100+).
mcp_notes: Official hosted remote server https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp (Streamable HTTP); consent screen issues an MCP-scoped API key, or manually generated MCP key; Enterprise can use existing keys. Paid plans Lite+; draws from the same API unit allowance. No local/GitHub version mentioned.
blocker: Needs paid Lite+ plan; OAuth requires Ahrefs Connect approval
notes: 'Sandbox' here means free test queries on fixed targets only, not a separate environment. Ahrefs Connect (OAuth for third-party apps, end users need Lite+) requires applying with product description and app review before going live; a third-party-cited docs page suggests production integrations need Enterprise (not verified). Fetch failures: docs.ahrefs.com/docs/api/reference/introduction and docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/introduction both returned 404. Older help translations say API is Enterprise-only; current English help says Lite+.

one_liner: AI web scraping service: HTML/markdown/JSON extraction, screenshots, web search, scraper workflows.
auth_notes: API token created in dashboard (profile menu > API Tokens) with a name and expiration date; sent in 'x-api-token' header. Marketplace endpoints use 'Authorization: Bearer'. Base URL https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1. Hosted MCP uses OAuth 2.1 (scrape:read, account:read) or API key as bearer.
access_notes: Scraper Free plan, no credit card (token allowance stated inconsistently as 100/month in text vs 1,000 in table; 10 concurrent requests, no residential proxies). Pro (200K tokens) and Enterprise paid. Docs do not explicitly restrict API tokens by plan but also do not explicitly confirm API on Free.
api_breadth_notes: ~5 scraping endpoints (Web Search, Scrape HTML, Scrape Markdown, Screenshot, Scrape JSON/Brand) plus platform endpoints (workflow rerun, cancel bulk scraping, results, analytics, subscription account). Well under 20.
mcp_notes: Official server: hosted https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 or API key) and local npm @mrscraper/mcp (stdio/HTTP, MRSCRAPER_API_KEY). Source github.com/mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp. 7 tools: status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, webSearch.
notes: Webhook support is a 'Webhook integration' that pushes scraper results to external URLs (listed on docs home; detail page not opened). Rate limits not documented on the API overview. The docs page for 'Token Plan' (getting-started/api-token) contained no creation details; the API Authentication page did. Prices not shown on billing page.

one_liner: Cloud platform to run scrapers/automation 'Actors', with storage, scheduling and an Actor marketplace.
auth_notes: Personal API token (Console > Settings > API & Integrations), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (or ?token= param, discouraged). Tokens can be scoped to specific resources and given expiry. Integration docs list OAuth 2.0 for third-party integrations, but client registration process is not documented (contact integrations@apify.com). Also x402/Skyfire agentic payment auth.
access_notes: Free plan at $0 with $5 of monthly platform usage, no credit card required; token available immediately. Usage beyond credit blocked until next cycle or paid plan.
api_breadth_notes: API v2 with ~52 reference pages across Actors (versions, builds, runs, tasks, webhooks), Schedules, Storage (datasets, key-value stores, request queues), Webhooks, Store, Users, Logs, Tools; plus a Runtime API. Well over 100 operations. Thousands of Store Actors callable via the same run endpoints.
mcp_notes: Official hosted server https://mcp.apify.com (Streamable HTTP; OAuth recommended or Bearer token) and local npx @apify/actors-mcp-server (APIFY_TOKEN). Source github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server. Tool categories: actors, docs, runs, storage, tasks, schedules, builds, versions, api.
notes: No separate sandbox environment documented; the free plan's $5 monthly credit is sufficient for testing. Rate limits: 250K req/min global, default 60 req/s per resource; 429 with backoff. Official JS/Python clients handle retries. OAuth availability for third-party apps confirmed only at a high level (docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/integrate); obtaining client credentials appears to require contacting Apify.

one_liner: Web data API for AI: scrape, crawl, map, search, extract and browser agents to LLM-ready output.
auth_notes: API key (fc-...) sent as 'Authorization: Bearer'. 'OAuth for apps' flow for third-party integrations returns fco_ access tokens (usable on REST API) and single-use fcr_ refresh tokens; client registration process not described on the auth page. MCP OAuth tokens work only on the MCP server. Some endpoints have keyless limited use.
access_notes: Free plan: 1,000 credits/month (renewing), no credit card, 2 concurrent requests, low rate limits (e.g. 10/min scrape/map/search, 2/min crawl/agent). Paid plans raise limits.
api_breadth_notes: ~50 v2 endpoint pages: Search, Scrape/Batch Scrape, Interact (browser sessions), Map, Parse, Crawl, Monitor, Agent, Research/Developer/Government indexes, Account/credit usage; plus 13 webhook payload types.
mcp_notes: Official repo github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server (npm firecrawl-mcp, local stdio/HTTP) and hosted https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (Bearer API key) and /v2/mcp-oauth (OAuth sign-in); ~34 tools in full profile; keyless tier for scrape/search/parse.
notes: Open-source core can be self-hosted (MCP supports FIRECRAWL_API_URL for self-hosted instance); self-hosting docs not opened. The api-reference/introduction page still shows /v1 paths; use v2 endpoints. 'Firecrawl for Platforms' is a separate program for platforms that provision accounts for their users. 'Browser Sandbox'/Interact is a product feature, not a test environment.

one_liner: Web data platform: proxies, unblocker, SERP API, scraper APIs, scraping browser and datasets.
auth_notes: API key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'; keys created by account admins only (one per user) with permission level (Admin/Finance/Ops/Limit/User) and optional expiry. 'Native access' uses proxy username (brd-customer-<id>-zone-<zone>) + zone password for proxies, Web Unlocker and Scraping Browser. No OAuth documented.
access_notes: New accounts get 5,000 free credits/month (reset monthly, no credit card) shared across Web Unlocker, SERP API, Web Scraper API, Scraper Studio, Browser API and MCP. Proxies not in free tier (one-time $2 trial + $5 bonus after adding payment method). Unfunded accounts limited to 1,000 req/min.
api_breadth_notes: API references: Web Unlocker, SERP, Scraper API (sync/async trigger, progress, snapshots), Scraper Studio, Account management (zones etc.), Dataset Marketplace, plus Business Search endpoints. Exact endpoint count not given; hundreds of prebuilt scraper dataset IDs sit behind a few generic endpoints.
mcp_notes: Official server documented by Bright Data; source github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp; hosted remote https://mcp.brightdata.com/sse?token=API_KEY (SSE) or self-hosted local; tool groups selectable (e.g. groups=scrapers,browser); uses the 5,000/month free pool.
notes: Webhooks = Scraper API data delivery to a webhook/S3 (docs page listed in llms.txt, not opened). brightdata.com/pricing did not state free tier details; the docs free-tier page did. Fetching docs.brightdata.com/api-reference/introduction returned the authentication page content. Many products require creating a 'zone' first; API keys need admin role. Any KYC requirements for certain targets were not verified.

one_liner: Open-source CLI that finds social media accounts by username across 400+ sites.
auth_notes: No authentication: a local Python CLI (pipx install sherlock-project, Docker sherlock/sherlock). It makes unauthenticated requests to public sites; optional proxy support.
access_notes: MIT-licensed open-source tool; free to install and run, but no hosted API or web service is offered by the project.
api_breadth_notes: Single capability: username lookup across 400+ sites, with output to txt/CSV/XLSX and site filtering options.
mcp_notes: No official MCP. Community: Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp (local stdio FastMCP wrapper, one tool search_username, wraps the CLI as subprocess); other OSINT bundles and third-party Apify actors wrap Sherlock, unaffiliated with the project.
blocker: Local CLI only; toolkit must host its own execution runtime
notes: Facts are high-confidence; the verdict depends on whether a sandboxed CLI/Python runner counts as buildable (it would be 'blocked' under a strict no-API reading). Runs can be slow (community MCP uses 300s timeout) and results can include false positives; site list changes often. Consider ethical/ToS review for OSINT use.

one_liner: B2B contact and company enrichment aggregating 30+ data vendors for emails and phones.
auth_notes: API key in 'x-api-key' header against https://api.waterfall.io. Master API key can create/manage sub-keys via API Key Management endpoint. No OAuth documented.
access_notes: No self-serve signup documented; docs say to contact support@waterfall.io for API access and pricing, and the website offers 'Book a Call'. Usage-based pricing, no free trial mentioned.
api_breadth_notes: 13 endpoints: Prospector, Search Contact, Search Company (preview), Contact/Phone/Company Enrichment (async), Company Reveal (IP), Company Titles, Job Change, Email Verification, Webhook JWKS, Account Reporting, API Key Management.
mcp_notes: No MCP server in docs; Waterfall publishes agent skills (waterfall-direct-api, waterfall-integration) at github.com/Waterfall-io/api-skills. Community MCP servers not searched exhaustively.
blocker: API keys only via contacting Waterfall sales/support
notes: Async jobs return job_id: poll the Finder endpoint or receive signed (Ed25519, JWKS-verifiable) results at webhook_url; SUCCEEDED does not guarantee all fields found. 402 when over quota. Gate is really 'become a customer via sales' rather than a formal partnership; docs and OpenAPI spec are public, so a toolkit using end-user keys is buildable once a test key is obtained.

one_liner: GTM data platform: people/company search, enrichment waterfalls, tables, and AI-driven workflows.
auth_notes: Personal API key in 'clay-api-key' header; base https://api.clay.com/public/v0. Keys created in app (API and CLI > API keys) or via 'clay api-keys create'; tied to a user and their workspace access. No OAuth for the Public API (Clay's MCP for reps uses OAuth tokens).
access_notes: Pricing page shows 'Build via CLI / API' on all plans: Free (100 search results/30 days, 500 actions + 100 data credits/mo), Launch and Growth (1M/30 days), Enterprise (10M). Tables API is Enterprise-only; HTTP API integrations and webhook signals are Growth+.
api_breadth_notes: ~18 Public API endpoints: Search (6), Routines (5), Audiences (2), Workflow runs beta (2), Tables (1, Enterprise), Credits (1), Me (1).
mcp_notes: Clay-hosted MCP ('MCP for reps') connected via OAuth from Claude/ChatGPT/Glean/M365 Copilot; admin invites Sales Rep users, sets credit limits, and enables Functions/workflows for MCP. Server URL not listed on the settings page.
blocker: Tiny free quota; Tables API Enterprise-only; API still v0
notes: Public API is new (v0); Workflows are Alpha and Workflow runs beta. Webhooks are outbound only for routine runs, registered via CLI ('clay webhooks create'), HMAC-signed (X-Clay-Signature), delivery not guaranteed. Older community posts say Clay had no public API; they predate the current developer platform. Plan-gating of API key creation not stated in auth docs; inferred from pricing table.
